Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Billing for multi-entity deployment — VAT handling question

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Aurelia is excited to move forward with the private deployment for two of our business units (Aurelia Clinics and Aurelia Research). Before we lock the purchase order, procurement needs clarity on how invoices will be split across our legal entities and how VAT will be handled.

Specifically: 
- We need invoices split by legal entity (Aurelia Clinics Ltd, Aurelia Research LLC) with separate net lines for seat-by-seat charges and a consolidated tax summary.
- For EU VAT, we need to confirm whether Redwood can issue separate VAT-charged invoices per entity, or whether Aurelia should manage VAT reconciliation via a VAT delegation/MOU.
- Any recommended invoice layout that maps to our GL/account codes would be super helpful to accelerate AP.

Can you share a sample mapping and indicate whether there are any additional procurement steps (DocuSign, supplier setup) we should anticipate?

Best,
Maria
Maria Gomez
Head of Procurement
Aurelia Health

--
Aurelia Health (procurement@aureliahealth.com)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@aureliahealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Billing for multi-entity deployment — VAT handling question

Hi Maria — thanks for the clear list.

Short answers up front: we can support per-entity invoices with seat-level breakdowns and a consolidated tax summary. For EU VAT, we typically do one of two approaches: Redwood issues VAT invoices per billed legal entity (if the entity is the contracting/paying party and has a VAT ID), or we execute a VAT delegation MOU where Aurelia will self-account for VAT and Redwood issues net invoices. Both are supported; the choice depends on your AP and tax preference.

I attached a quick mapping XSLX that maps our invoice lines to common GL codes and shows a sample split across two entities. I also attached a draft VAT delegation MOU template for your tax team to review.

Next steps I propose: 
1) You confirm which legal entities will be the invoiced parties and provide VAT IDs where relevant.
2) If you want Redwood to issue VAT invoices per entity, confirm billing addresses and remit instructions.
3) If you prefer VAT delegation, have your tax counsel review the MOU and flag any changes.

I'll loop in Laura from Finance to confirm what fields we can include on each invoice (PO number, cost centers, custom fields). Ben from Customer Ops will outline our supplier onboarding checklist (DocuSign, W9/EU equivalents). If it's helpful I can also propose a short mutual action plan with dates.

Thanks — we'll aim to keep this as low friction as possible.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposed-invoice-mapping.xlsx, vat-delegation-mou-draft.pdf
From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 08:25:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Billing for multi-entity deployment — VAT handling question

Karthik / Ben / Priyom — forwarding Maria's note and Karthik's reply. Quick internal notes from Finance: 

- We can generate separate invoices per legal entity and include a custom cost center field (up to 4-6 characters) that maps to customer GLs. Recommend we ask Aurelia for a PO per entity to keep collections clean.
- For VAT: if they want Redwood to charge VAT (we issue VAT invoices), we need validated VAT IDs and their supplier profile set up in our billing system. If they prefer delegation, the MOU needs: confirmation of self-accounting registration number, effective date, and whether they want consolidated monthly statements versus entity-level statements.
- On credits/chargebacks: if a refund needs apportioning across entities, we prefer a proportional credit method tied to the invoice line allocation; we'll document the formula in the MOU.

Priyom — any technical constraints on invoice line length or extra fields for export to our ingestion pipeline?
Thanks,
Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Finance | Redwood Inference

--
Note: internal: include standard fiscal terms (Net 30) and our AP contact: ap@redwood.ai
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Billing for multi-entity deployment — VAT handling question

Laura — technically we can support up to 8 custom metadata fields on each invoice line (freeform, but we recommend using a constrained code list). Exchange format: CSV/MT940 export for their ERP ingestion; we can also provide a mapping CSV that matches our invoice_line_id to their GL code.

Two operational notes: 
1) If Aurelia requests consolidated monthly statements plus separate entity invoices, that increases reconciliation overhead. Recommend consolidated statements only if they accept the separate-entity invoices for payment routing.
2) For proportional credits we need the split logic codified (percent by seats or by spend) — otherwise refunds become manual. We should propose the proportional-by-seat default and allow them to request an alternate formula.

I can produce the mapping CSV once Maria confirms entity names and VAT IDs.

— Priyom
Senior Billing Engineer | Redwood Inference

Hi Maria — looping back with a proposed mutual action plan and attachments.

Summary of agreed options: 
- Redwood can issue per-entity invoices with seat-level lines and a cost_center custom field. If Aurelia provides PO and VAT ID per entity, Redwood will apply VAT where required.
- Alternatively, Aurelia can sign the VAT delegation MOU; Redwood will then issue net invoices and Aurelia will self-account for VAT.

Attached: proposed-invoice-mapping.xlsx (example mapping and sample PDFs), vat-delegation-mou-draft.pdf (editable draft).

Proposed immediate timeline (high level):
1) By 2027-06-07 — Aurelia to confirm invoiced entities + VAT IDs and provide PO template or indicate preference for MOU.
2) By 2027-06-11 — Redwood sends finalized invoice templates and mapping CSV for their ERP ingestion.
3) By 2027-06-18 — Supplier onboarding complete (DocuSign, tax docs), first invoices issued for June usage (prorated as needed).

If this works, I'll open a short “billing kickoff” session (30 min) to finalize PO fields and cost_center codes — propose 2027-06-08 or 2027-06-09.

Thanks — happy to adjust the timeline.

Best regards,
Karthik Iyer
